key_insight: In small exact simulations, fixed-angle QASPA-MaxCut achieved mean best-of-four selection ratios of 0.955–1.000, exceeding the reported mean expected ratios of depth-one QAOA.
engineering_relevance: The results motivate evaluating classical selection and optimizer-restart budgets alongside circuit depth when designing shallow quantum Max-Cut solvers.
method: Encode graph edges with CX–Ry(θ)–CX shift-phase blocks.
Evaluate the four leading QASPA bit strings classically and retain the best cut.
Compare one-layer QASPA with depth-one QAOA optimized over one to ten restarts.
evidence_signal: Seed-42 state-vector tests covered backbone-augmented random graphs at four additional-edge probabilities and 19 custom unweighted topologies; retained finite-shot checks preserved topology-level readout.
watch_item: QASPA best-of-four selection and QAOA expected-value scoring are different metrics, so the reported gap does not establish quantum advantage or hardware scalability.
paper_title: QASPA-MaxCut on Unweighted Graphs: Edge Encoding and QAOA Restarts
